title: Title Case a Sentence
prompt: A publishing tool formats simple headlines. Write a function that returns the sentence with the first letter of each space-separated word capitalized and the rest of each word left unchanged.

explanation.beginner:
Example: titleCase("hello world") produces "Hello World". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “handles a longer sentence”: input ["the lazy brown dog"] produces "The Lazy Brown Dog". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

The reference uses split, map, slice, join. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles a longer sentence”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
